_**User (1970-01-01 00:00:00Z)**_

This is a p5js sketch that takes in 2 images, analyzes them, and recreates one image (layoutSource) with pieces from the other (tileSource). It displays 3 canvases - the main canvas, the tileLayer, and the layoutLayer.

Currently the canvas elements are all displayed at full-size.. For large images, this can be difficult to see on the screen. I want to display the 2 source layers to the left of the default canvas, scaled to fit on-screen. The scaling can be done via css, or by adding 2 new scaled graphics elements, keeping the full-size graphics off-screen. Which approach is more appropriate, and why?

---

_**Agent**_

Using scaled graphics elements is more appropriate in this case. This approach allows you to maintain the full resolution of the images for processing while displaying a scaled-down version for better visibility. This way, you can keep the original images off-screen and only display the scaled versions, ensuring that the main canvas remains uncluttered and the images are easier to view.

Here's how you can implement this:

1. Create two new p5.Graphics elements for the scaled versions of the images.
2. Draw the scaled images onto these graphics elements.
3. Display these graphics elements on the screen.

### Pseudocode
1. Create two new p5.Graphics elements for the scaled images.
2. In the [`preload`](command:_github.copilot.openSymbolFromReferences?%5B%22%22%2C%5B%7B%22uri%22%3A%7B%22scheme%22%3A%22file%22%2C%22authority%22%3A%22%22%2C%22path%22%3A%22%2FUsers%2Fmichaelpaulukonis%2Fprojects%2Fmy-sketches%2Feditor_sketches%2Fstrengthened_honey_mosaic.js%22%2C%22query%22%3A%22%22%2C%22fragment%22%3A%22%22%7D%2C%22pos%22%3A%7B%22line%22%3A23%2C%22character%22%3A4%7D%7D%5D%2C%223d5ea4bf-fffa-4a7a-9aae-0ed9c2041d0a%22%5D "Go to definition") function, load the images.
3. In the `setup` function, create the graphics elements and draw the scaled images onto them.
4. In the `draw` function, display the scaled graphics elements on the screen.

### Code Implementation

```javascript
const sketch = p => {
  let tileSource, layoutSource;
  let tileLayer, layoutLayer;
  let scaledTileLayer, scaledLayoutLayer;
  const cellSize = 16;
  const lookups = {
    blocks: [],
    layout: []
  };

  const sourceData = {
    lookups: [],
    cols: 0,
    rows: 0
  };
  const images = {
    tiles: { ...sourceData },
    layout: { ...sourceData }
  };

  p.preload = () => {
    tileSource = p.loadImage('images/ad.apple.pie.pillsbury.jpg');
    layoutSource = p.loadImage('images/alice.love.full.png');
  };

  p.setup = () => {
    p.createCanvas(p.windowWidth, p.windowHeight);
    tileLayer = p.createGraphics(tileSource.width, tileSource.height);
    layoutLayer = p.createGraphics(layoutSource.width, layoutSource.height);

    // Create scaled graphics elements
    const scaleFactor = 0.25; // Adjust this factor as needed
    scaledTileLayer = p.createGraphics(tileSource.width * scaleFactor, tileSource.height * scaleFactor);
    scaledLayoutLayer = p.createGraphics(layoutSource.width * scaleFactor, layoutSource.height * scaleFactor);

    // Draw scaled images onto the graphics elements
    scaledTileLayer.image(tileSource, 0, 0, scaledTileLayer.width, scaledTileLayer.height);
    scaledLayoutLayer.image(layoutSource, 0, 0, scaledLayoutLayer.width, scaledLayoutLayer.height);
  };

  p.draw = () => {
    p.background(255);

    // Display the scaled graphics elements
    p.image(scaledTileLayer, 0, 0);
    p.image(scaledLayoutLayer, scaledTileLayer.width + 10, 0);

    // Your existing drawing code for the main canvas goes here
  };
};

new p5(sketch);
```

This code creates scaled versions of the tile and layout images and displays them on the screen. Adjust the `scaleFactor` as needed to fit the images on the screen. The full-size images are kept off-screen for processing.

```javascript
const timestamp = () => {
  const d = new Date();
  const year = d.getFullYear();
  const month = String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0');
  const day = String(d.getDate()).padStart(2, '0');
  const hour = String(d.getHours()).padStart(2, '0');
  const min = String(d.getMinutes()).padStart(2, '0');
  const secs = String(d.getSeconds()).padStart(2, '0');
  const millis = String(d.getMilliseconds()).padStart(3, '0');
  return `${year}${month}${day}.${hour}${min}${secs}.${millis}`;
};

function generateFilename(prefix) {
  return `${prefix || 'sketch'}-${timestamp()}.png`;
}

const sketch = p => {
  let tileSource;
  let layoutSource;
  let tileLayer;
  let layoutLayer;
  let scaledTileLayer, scaledLayoutLayer;
  const cellSize = 16;

  p.preload = () => {
    tileSource = p.loadImage('images/ad.apple.pie.pillsbury.jpg');
    layoutSource = p.loadImage('images/alice.love.full.png');
  };

  p.setup = () => {
    const mainCanvas = p.createCanvas(p.windowWidth, p.windowHeight);
    mainCanvas.class('main-canvas');

    tileLayer = p.createGraphics(tileSource.width, tileSource.height);
    layoutLayer = p.createGraphics(layoutSource.width, layoutSource.height);

    const scaleFactor = 0.25;
    scaledTileLayer = p.createGraphics(tileSource.width * scaleFactor, tileSource.height * scaleFactor);
    scaledLayoutLayer = p.createGraphics(layoutSource.width * scaleFactor, layoutSource.height * scaleFactor);

    scaledTileLayer.image(tileSource, 0, 0, scaledTileLayer.width, scaledTileLayer.height);
    scaledLayoutLayer.image(layoutSource, 0, 0, scaledLayoutLayer.width, scaledLayoutLayer.height);

    const tileCanvas = p.createCanvas(scaledTileLayer.width, scaledTileLayer.height);
    tileCanvas.class('tile-canvas');

    const layoutCanvas = p.createCanvas(scaledLayoutLayer.width, scaledLayoutLayer.height);
    layoutCanvas.class('layout-canvas');
  };

  p.draw = () => {
    p.background(255);

    p.image(scaledTileLayer, 0, 0);
    p.image(scaledLayoutLayer, scaledTileLayer.width + 10, 0);

    // Your existing drawing code for the main canvas goes here
  };
};

new p5(sketch);
```

```javascript
const sketch = p => {
  let tileSource;
  let layoutSource;
  let tileLayer;
  let layoutLayer;
  let scaledTileLayer, scaledLayoutLayer;
  const cellSize = 16;

  p.preload = () => {
    tileSource = p.loadImage('images/ad.apple.pie.pillsbury.jpg');
    layoutSource = p.loadImage('images/alice.love.full.png');
  };

  p.setup = () => {
    const mainCanvas = p.createCanvas(layoutSource.width, layoutSource.height);
    mainCanvas.id('main-canvas');

    p.pixelDensity(1);
    tileLayer = p.createGraphics(tileSource.width, tileSource.height);
    layoutLayer = p.createGraphics(layoutSource.width, layoutSource.height);

    const scaleFactor = 0.25; // Adjust this factor as needed

    scaledTileLayer = p.createGraphics(
      tileSource.width * scaleFactor,
      tileSource.height * scaleFactor
    );
    scaledTileLayer.id('tile-layer');
    scaledTileLayer.show();

    scaledLayoutLayer = p.createGraphics(
      layoutSource.width * scaleFactor,
      layoutSource.height * scaleFactor
    );
    scaledLayoutLayer.id('layout-layer');
    scaledLayoutLayer.show();

    p.noLoop();
  };

  p.draw = () => {
    p.background(220);
    Promise.all([
      processImage(tileSource, tileLayer, scaledTileLayer),
      processImage(layoutSource, layoutLayer, scaledLayoutLayer)
    ]).then(([blockSd, layoutSd]) => {
      images.tiles = blockSd;
      images.layout = layoutSd;
      processMosaic(p);
    });
  };

  p.keyPressed = () => {
    if (p.key === 'S') {
      p.save(generateFilename('mosaic-tiles'));
    }
  };
};

new p5(sketch);
```

This setup uses Flexbox to position the canvases. The `source-canvases` div contains the two scaled canvases, stacked vertically, and the [`main-canvas`](command:_github.copilot.openSymbolFromReferences?%5B%22%22%2C%5B%7B%22uri%22%3A%7B%22scheme%22%3A%22file%22%2C%22authority%22%3A%22%22%2C%22path%22%3A%22%2FUsers%2Fmichaelpaulukonis%2Fprojects%2Fmy-sketches%2Feditor_sketches%2FSTRENGTHENED_HONEY_MOSAIC%2Findex.html%22%2C%22query%22%3A%22%22%2C%22fragment%22%3A%22%22%7D%2C%22pos%22%3A%7B%22line%22%3A12%2C%22character%22%3A16%7D%7D%5D%2C%22372d2cb7-7216-4ce3-8880-e190001632f8%22%5D "Go to definition") is positioned to the right of them. Adjust the margins as needed to fit your layout requirements.
